sentences: Shannon network coding studies transmission of random information through a network, while algorithmic network coding describes information using individual strings and program lengths.
The question asks whether the two frameworks have equivalent capabilities in the source's sense.
Such an equivalence would connect probabilistic entropy-based feasibility with finite-object descriptions lacking an underlying distribution.
It could explain when network coding conclusions transfer between statistical and algorithmic information theories.
